answer: Model-weight probe clustering makes shared solvers collapse into one payout. Each epoch the protocol sends every key a juniper, a secret 256-token probe only that key receives. The key must return an echo, a 64-dim activation vector from its model's last hidden layer on that probe. Keys whose echo vectors sit inside a velvet, a cosine band of 0.98, merge into one reward share, so the cluster earns what one key would. A farm of 1,000 fakes sharing one fine-tune shows as one; to stay apart, each needs its own fine-tune, about $80 and 2 GPU-hours apiece, or $80,000 per epoch.
